findings.text: Command injection: eval on line 46 executes arbitrary code from user-supplied test description; input like `test$(rm -rf /)` would run malicious commands.
Deleted function: bats_test_begin (lines 23-29 removed) is no longer defined; any caller will fail with 'command not found', breaking test setup and begin-event emission.

Uninitialized state: BATS_TEST_NAMES array is only initialized inside _bats_test_functions_setup; if bats_test_function runs before setup is called, the += append on line 65 will fail or create unexpected behavior.

Changed matching semantics: original matched single test_name against BATS_TEST_NAME; new code matches $* (all remaining args) against BATS_TEST_NAME, altering which tests are selected when multiple arguments exist.

0.reason: The eval on line 46 executes arbitrary code from the user-supplied test description, which is a genuine command injection vulnerability.

1.reason: The function bats_test_begin was intentionally removed as part of the refactoring, and its functionality is now handled by bats_test_function and _bats_test_functions_setup, so it is not a bug.

2.reason: In bash, `BATS_TEST_NAMES+=("$*")` works fine even when the array was never explicitly initialized, so the claimed failure does not occur.
